newsitem.title: INDIA: Inmarsat in pact with India on satellite telephony.
newsitem.headline: Inmarsat in pact with India on satellite telephony.

text.p: Inmarsat has signed an agreement with India's Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to start a pilot project to provide satellite phone services at 100 remote sites in India, a company official said on Thursday.

"We have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with DoT to undertake a pilot project initially looking at 100 sites which are in remote or inaccessible areas to provide Inmarsat communications facilities," Bashir Patel told Reuters in an interview.

Patel is the regional director for central and western Asia in Inmarsat, currently the world's only provider of global mobile satellite communications. It is a multinational cooperative of 79 countries based in London.
The pilot project in India will run for a year, said Patel.
The project was aimed at communities in far-flung areas which do not have basic telephone services but need communication services for their economic and other activities.

"We are looking at rural communities which for their day to day life or for their economic activity require communication services. And therefore there will be reasonable usage of the service," Patel said.
The satellite services can also be used at sites in remote areas where infrastructure facilities like power plants, bridges and mines are being built, he said.
"Once the pilot project is complete and we find there are certain categories of sites which are economically viable then there will be a facility or telephone installed," Patel said.
Patel said the potential for using satellite telephone systems for remote area communication was immense.

"DoT will be able to find 5,000 to 10,000 sites in northern India where they will be able to install the systems and allow the community in that area to use it to the extent that it will pay for itself," Patel said.
The company was also in talks with local firms for supply of components for its satellite phone systems, Patel added.
